title: What Digital Farming Tools Does a Modern Filipino Farm Need?
metaTitle: Digital Farming Tools a Modern Filipino Farm Needs
metaDescription: The digital farming tools a Filipino farm needs: records, weather, fertilizer and variety advice, prices and RSBSA. Most are free and run on a phone.
excerpt: A modern Filipino farm needs six digital farming tools: a planning and records app, a weather and typhoon tracker, a fertilizer adviser, a variety guide, a pest and disease helper, and a way to check prices and reach buyers. Most of them are free and run on an ordinary smartphone. Built for Filipino farmers, the anee.io farm app covers planning, records, weather and pest help in one place. It works best beside free government tools such as RCMAS, Binhing Palay and PAGASA's agri weather.

blocks.text:
Going digital does not start with drones or sensors. It starts with the phone already in your pocket. The right tools save trips to town, catch problems early and keep records you can show a lender, a buyer or the DA.

Below is the short list, what each tool does, the free options from government agencies, and where anee.io fits. Use what you need and skip the rest.

items: Start with three: a farm record app, PAGASA's agri weather and your RSBSA registration.
Get fertilizer and variety advice from free government tools, RCMAS and the Binhing Palay app.
Check prices before you sell, using the DA's price monitoring page and your own buyer records.
One farm app can hold the plan, costs, weather and pest help, so you do not juggle five notebooks.

blocks.text: What the free government tools give you

items: **PAGASA Agri Weather** posts farm weather forecasts, ten day regional agri weather information and tropical cyclone warnings for agriculture.
**RCMAS** is a free service that gives crop and nutrient advice for your own field. DA offices, the Agricultural Training Institute and local extension workers run it.
**Binhing Palay** is a catalogue of released rice varieties. You filter it by location, environment, season and crop establishment, and it works offline.
**DA Price Monitoring** publishes weekly average retail prices and a daily price index.

blocks.text: What should you set up first?

items.title: Register in the RSBSA
items.text: It is the DA's list of farmers, farm workers and fisherfolk, and it is how the government finds beneficiaries for its programs. Registration is free and lasts a lifetime.

items.title: Save PAGASA Agri Weather on your phone
items.text: Check the farm forecast before every spray, and the cyclone warnings for agriculture in typhoon season.

items.title: Start a farm record on one lot
items.text: Write what you did, what you spent and what you harvested. A free app like anee.io's Libre plan or a notebook both work, as long as you keep it up.

items.title: Ask for fertilizer advice
items.text: Ask your extension worker for an RCMAS recommendation before your first fertilizer application.

items.title: Add tools as the farm grows
items.text: Workers, inventory and full reports matter once you hire help and keep a shed of inputs.

blocks.text:
To register in the RSBSA, you must be a Filipino citizen, at least 18 years old, and a farmer, farm worker, fisherfolk or agri youth. Get the enrollment form from your City or Municipal Agriculture Office. Bring a valid government ID and proof of land ownership, tenancy or lease. You then receive a stub with a temporary RSBSA control number.

Once registered, you can apply for DA programs such as agricultural loans, crop and livestock insurance, seeds, fertilizer, technical help and soil analysis.

blocks.title: A dated photo is a record
blocks.text: Snap the receipt, the sacks on the scale and the flooded field on the day it happens. Your phone stamps the date. When a lender, an insurer or a buyer asks what happened, a photo from that day settles it faster than memory.

blocks.title: Put the whole season on one app
blocks.text: Start free on one lot. anee.io keeps the plan, the costs, the weather and the harvest together.

blocks.text: Do you need drones and sensors to farm digitally?

Not to start. Satellites already pass over Philippine farms, and an app can read them for you. In anee.io, Satellite Analysis has Anee read the newest Sentinel 2 picture and Sentinel 1 radar of your drawn field. Radar sees through typhoon clouds, so the reading still works in the rainy season. It uses credits.

Read more in our guides to [satellite images of your farm](/blog/satellite-crop-monitoring-philippines) and [monitoring crop health without a drone](/blog/monitor-crop-health-without-a-drone). A drone or a soil sensor can come later, once your records show where the money is lost. Most of the crop production tools above are free. When you are ready for hardware, see our guide to [farm sensors in the Philippines](/blog/farm-sensors-philippines).
How does anee.io fit into a digital farm?

anee.io puts the planning, records and field help in one app that runs in any phone browser and keeps working without signal. The [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) dates every task, and the [NPK Plus calculator](/features/npk-plus-calculator) checks a fertilizer plan. The [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) name active ingredients, never brands. In The Stash, you can read every PhilRice Magazine issue inside the app.

Be clear on the limits too. Anee needs internet and uses credits. The free Libre plan has ads, one active season and one lot. NPK Plus and the finders start at Libre plus Anee, and workers and inventory at Solo Farmer.

items.q: What is the most important digital tool for a small farmer?
items.a: A simple record of what you did, what you spent and what you harvested. Without it, no other tool can tell you if the season paid. Start with one lot and keep it up for a full season.

items.q: Are there free digital farming tools in the Philippines?
items.a: Yes. PAGASA Agri Weather, the Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service, the Binhing Palay app and the DA's price monitoring page cost nothing. On anee.io, the Libre plan is free too.

items.q: Do these tools work without internet?
items.a: Some do. The Binhing Palay app works offline, and anee.io keeps working without signal on every plan, then syncs. Weather updates and Anee's answers need a connection.

items.q: How do I register in the RSBSA?
items.a: Get the enrollment form from your City or Municipal Agriculture Office and fill it out. Bring a valid government ID and proof of land ownership, tenancy or lease. Registration is free, and you receive a stub with a temporary control number.

items.q: Can I use a farm app in Tagalog?
items.a: Yes. Anee, the smart farm technician inside anee.io, answers in Tagalog, Bisaya, Ilocano, Taglish or English. You can ask in your own words and send a photo of the problem.
